verdict.rationale: First-party docs state that Obsidian stores notes as non-proprietary, plain-text Markdown files locally so users can switch apps easily ([obsidian-docs-20], [obsidian-docs-2], [obsidian-docs-23]). Community sources independently confirm that the files outlive the app and that the format is future-proof ([obsidian-comm-19], [obsidian-comm-3], [obsidian-comm-20]), and Canvas uses an MIT-licensed open JSON format ([obsidian-comm-14]); one user's concern about JSON readability ([obsidian-comm-15]) is not a contradiction. missing for 10: evidence of a documented spec for Obsidian-specific Markdown extensions (wikilinks, embeds) and for the on-disk format of newer features such as Bases.
